scope: chat:which crops are affected by the expansion?

gemini.value:
The passages state that crops threatened by the Mexican fruit fly in California include peach, avocado, orange, grapefruit, and pear [cdfa_mexfly_page#000], as well as apple, Meyer lemon, sweet lime, mandarin, nectarine, Japanese persimmon, pomegranate, and tangerine [cdfa_pep_sv_amd2#013]. Regulated host plant species also include papaya, apple chili, custard-apple, and white sapote [mexfly_hosts#013]. Quarantine areas in San Diego County include Spring Valley and El Cajon (effective June 18, 2026) [cdfa_pep_sv_amd2#003] and La Mesa (effective August 14, 2026) [cdfa_mexfly_page#000].

The sources don't settle this. They do not detail exact crop-by-crop impacts specific to a particular boundary expansion beyond general threatened crop and host lists. You must confirm specific commodity status and current boundary impacts with CDFA, the San Diego County Agricultural Commissioner, or USDA APHIS.

QUOTES: [{"chunk_id": "cdfa_mexfly_page#000", "quote": "A large number of commercially grown crops in California would be threatened by the introduction of this pest, including peach, avocado, orange, grapefruit and pear."}, {"chunk_id": "cdfa_pep_sv_amd2#013", "quote": "Many crops in California are threatened by the presence of this pest including apple, avocado, grapefruit, Meyer lemon, sweet lime, mandarin, nectarine, orange, peach, pear, Japanese persimmon, pomegranate, and tangerine."}]
